newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares seen scaling new heights this week.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares seen scaling new heights this week.

text.p: Solid macroeconomic fundamentals and strong year-end corporate earnings are expected to take Philippine shares to a record high, perhaps as early as this week, analysts said.
The market's composite index has been on a general ascent since the start of the year, settling at 3,332.53 on Friday.
That is 41.87 points shy of its record high of 3,375.90 last July. The surge then was powered by a falling inflation rate and strong first semester corporate earnings.

As the full-year reporting season approaches, analysts said on Saturday that the confluence of a positive macroeconomic outlook and anticipation of double-digit earnings growth of blue-chip companies should propel another rally.
"There's a ground swell for the Philippine markets," Noel Reyes, research director of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities, told Reuters.
"We expect the market to test the 3,375 all-time high," a Sun Hung Kai Securities market forecast for the week said.

The economy remains strong after five years of consecutive growth. The government has forecast the gross national product to grow by more than 7.1 percent in 1996 and set a target of 7.8 percent this year.
Inflation is seen slowing to 6.5 percent this year from an average of 8.4 percent last year, it has said.

The optimism was reflected by Moody's Investors Service, which said on Friday that the country's marcoeconomic fundamentals had led it to put the Philippine sovereign rating on a credit watch for a possible upgrade.

In a series of Reuters polls over this month, analysts have projected strong earnings growth for big-capitalised companies such as Ayala Corp, Ayala Land Inc, Benpres Holdings Corp and Manila Electric Co.
They have estimated 1996 net profit growth of Ayala Corp at 33 percent, Ayala Land at 37 percent, Benpres at 25 percent and Manila Electric at 18.5 percent, and predicted further gains this year.

Also, Ayala Corp and Benpres, both of which are heavily weighted on the index, are expected to rise further this week after consortiums they were associated with won two contracts in the $7.0 billion-privatisation of the Manila waterworks.
Analyst also said they saw the market reacting favourably to annual results of another blue-chip issue, food and beverage giant San Miguel Corp. The results are likely to be announced on Tuesday.
Although San Miguel's 1996 earnings are likely to be less than in 1995, the company could predict an upbeat performance this year, the analysts have said.

"With favourable corporate news and earnings expected to be released next week, company expansion projects under way, together with the continuous creation of business alliances, as well as a fundamentally sound economy, investors are provided reason to stay...in equities," Rosanna Tiosic, an analyst of BPI Securities Corp, said in a weekly report.
However, Anscor's Reyes cautioned that profit-takers might prevent the record high being set this week. "As we reach the all-time high, worry warts will start selling," he added.
However, he said the stock index would reach 3,600 by mid-year, and 3,800 by the end of the year.
